body:
Good point. But it wouldn't actually need to take `sysret` as an argument anymore, since the filter callback is called _before_ syscall execution and the value is therefore still undefined (see [declaration without initalization](https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/60533c6193ede6ce403e82d09d82ae2bc8fb423a/linux-user/syscall.c#L14639) and [passing to the callback via pointer](https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/60533c6193ede6ce403e82d09d82ae2bc8fb423a/linux-user/syscall.c#L14678)).

I'd personally have a bit of a preference for the `ControlFlow` enum then, as the semantics are a bit more in line of what the callback does. Even though that'd require returning either `Continue(())` or `Break(val)` where `val` is the `u64` return value (imho, `Some(val)` and `None` read a bit nicer but the semantics aren't as clear).
